### Fixed
- **klaus-gateway's egress reaches its stores: the platform's Valkey and the Kubernetes API** (giantswarm/agent-platform#443; a Cilium installation, 2026-09-14). The connectivity chart's two policies selecting the gateway pod (`-klausgateway-a2a-egress`: DNS and the agentgateway data plane on 8080; `-klausgateway-obo-egress`: `world` / `cluster` on 443 and 10443) put it in Cilium default-deny egress and neither named the Valkey pods or the `kube-apiserver` entity — the API's Service address is resolved by Cilium's socket-LB before the policy applies, so the `cluster` port rule never matched it. Every installation ran the shapes that never leave the pod (memory routing, the bolt link store, no controller), so nothing showed it until klaus-gateway 1.3.0's Secret link store (`klausGateway.obo.store: secret`, giantswarm/klaus-gateway#245) was switched on: the gateway crash-looped at start on `read secret …/klaus-gateway-obo-links: … context deadline exceeded` (not `forbidden`: the Role was there, the route was not) and was rolled back by hand after about 95 s of downtime; the Valkey routing store this release adds (`klausGateway.routing.store: valkey`, klaus-gateway 1.6.0, giantswarm/klaus-gateway#252) would have hung every binding write and the readiness probe the same way. A third policy, `-klausgateway-store-egress`, now renders exactly while a store or the controller reaches beyond the pod, one rule per store: the platform's Valkey pods (`agent-platform.valkey.podSelector`, the release namespace) on `valkey.valkey.service.port` with `routing.store: valkey` and the valkey component on — an out-of-band Valkey (the component off) gets no rule, its egress is the installation's; the `kube-apiserver` entity (cilium) / `networkPolicy.kubernetes.apiServerCIDR` (kubernetes) with `obo.store: secret` and OBO on, `routing.store: configmap` or `crd`, or `controller.enabled`; DNS as in the siblings (`agent-platform.klausGateway.valkeyEgress` / `apiServerEgress`; the keys are the klaus-gateway chart's, forwarded by the meta chart and read with that chart's defaults when unset). The default shape renders as before, byte for byte; the five policies selecting or targeting the pod now share one `agent-platform.klausGateway.fullname` helper. `make verify-klausgateway-netpol` asserts every gate (each store alone, both together, the port following the Service, the out-of-band Valkey, the Secret store with OBO off, the bolt routing store), both flavours, the selector following `klausGateway.fullnameOverride` and the off switches; `ci/test-klausgateway-store-values.yaml` lints the cilium render with both stores, `ci/test-netpol-kubernetes-values.yaml` the kubernetes one. Not reproducible in agentlab (`networkPolicy.enabled: false`, kind runs no Cilium): verified by render and the chart's CI; the live proof is a store switch on a Cilium installation (`hubble observe --verdict DROPPED` on the gateway pod stays empty). **No installation acts**: every one runs the default shape; a switch to `obo.store: secret` or `routing.store: valkey` needs this release first — UPGRADE.md.
